title: Retirement-account investors in a property with a loan: tax on debt-financed income (UBTI)
rule: An individual retirement account, though tax-exempt, owes tax on unrelated business taxable income. Income from debt-financed property counts in proportion to average acquisition debt over average adjusted basis; gain on a sale uses the highest acquisition debt in the 12 months before it, even if repaid. A partner includes its share of partnership income. The real-property debt exception covers listed qualified organizations, such as section 401 qualified trusts, not individual retirement accounts; its conditions reach a partnership's income allocations and can limit distribution terms. A $1,000 specific deduction applies; per the Form 990-T instructions, $1,000 or more of unrelated gross income requires a return. The tax is the account's.

citation.authority: 26 U.S.C. 408(e)(1), 511, 512(b)(4), (b)(12) and (c)(1), 514(a), (b)(1), (c)(7) and (c)(9)(B), (C) and (E); filing threshold: IRS Instructions for Form 990-T and Publication 598

changeWatch: Amendments to sections 511 to 514 (including the qualified-organization list in 514(c)(9)(C)), a revision of IRS Publication 598, or a change to the Form 990-T filing threshold.
